transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30 15:00 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Jordan Park, Rina Gupta (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Sofia Alvarez, Tom Becker, Elena Ruiz (Orion)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the canary results and then walk the cutover play. quick check, any new stakeholders?
[00:14] Priya (Orion): no new ones on my side, just want to make sure SLOs are in the mix today.
[00:18] Liam (Redwood): cool, i'll start with the telemetry summary, but caveat, ubuntu agent had a small clock skew so some timestamps may be off by a few seconds —
[00:28] Carlos (Orion): saw that, yes some traces showed odd gaps.
[00:31] Liam: right, so overall 5% traffic canary ran for 18 hours, we collected token-level latency and QPS. p50 stayed ~110ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 spikes to 980-1.2s during a KV cash hit — i mean KV cache miss storm, sorry transcription.
[00:50] Tom (Orion): KV cash — love that typo, but yes we saw that pattern when the cache warmed and then a regen happened.
[00:56] Rina (Redwood): a few clarifications: the regen correlated with the long-tailed prompts where sequence length jumped; our runtime didn't fully take advantage of prefix caching for those call paths.
[01:12] Priya: can you explain the prefix caching limitation? do we need to change prompt templates?
[01:18] Liam: so prefix/KV caching works best when users have repeated context or small shifts; for the bursty long prompts we saw full KV loads which bumps memory and evicts older entries — that causes extra token recompute. possible mitigations: tune cache TTLs, pin certain prefixes, or use model side batching changes.
[01:38] Priya: ok, what about cost? we ran budget sim against the p95 numbers and it blew the 20% over forecast.
[01:45] Maya: on cost, we're proposing two levers: quantize to 8-bit for non-critical routes and adjust batching windows for background vs interactive traffic. quantization gives about 30% token-cost reduction but may add 5-8% latency in small requests.
[02:02] Elena (Orion): latency tradeoffs are fine for embeddings and background scoring but for patient-facing chat we need p95 under 500ms.
[02:12] Liam: understood; so plan A: keep interactive on the non-quantized variant, route background to quantized. plan B: use dynamic routing by latency SLO where requests that cross Xms get routed to a faster dedicated pool.
[02:30] Sofia (Orion): quick sec — on dedicated pool, is that a separate infra or same model compiled differently? security needs to know the boundary.
[02:38] Maya: dedicated is isolated GPU pool with RBAC and optional VPC peering, you still use the same model artifacts but we provision reserved nodes. for audited environments, we can enable customer KMS and audit logs.
[02:49] Sofia: KMS — do you support HSM-backed keys? rotation windows?
[02:53] Liam: yes HSM via KMS provider integrations, rotation is configurable but there are constraints during snapshot restores we need to coordinate; we'll capture this in the security doc.
[03:05] Carlos: on the perf tests, we saw a steady p99 drop after enabling continuous batching by increasing the gather window — but at peak it seems to add 30-40ms to p50 which hurts interactive.
[03:20] Rina: that's expected; batching improves throughput but there's a latency tail. suggestion: use micro-batching for interactive (small gather window 8-12ms) and larger windows for background lanes.
[03:33] Maya: this is where routing + canary helps. we can run an A/B within the 5% canary to compare micro vs macro batching, and tie alarms to p95 drift.
[03:44] Priya: did we capture severity of user impact? how many user-facing requests were affected?
[03:49] Liam: about 12% of the canary requests were interactive user messages; those corresponded to most of the p99 spikes because of the long sequence prompts.
[03:58] Tom: we have a public holiday spike coming next week so want rollouts to be safe.
[04:03] Jordan (Redwood): ok, for the cutover play we'll propose a staged ramp: 1) internal smoke 0.1% 2) 1% for 6h 3) 5% for 18h with SLO gates 4) 20% for 12h 5) full shift. each stage has abort criteria on p99 > threshold, error rate > X, or CPU/GPU saturation.
[04:25] Elena: do we have the exact thresholds?
[04:28] Rina: suggested defaults: p95 < 500ms interactive, p99 < 1.0s interactive, error increase < 0.5% absolute, and a token cost delta within forecast +/- 15%. but those are negotiable.
[04:45] Priya: the cost delta is big for us, so we need a precomputed budget table per-stage.
[04:51] Maya: Liam will deliver a perf spreadsheet with projected token cost per stage — that is an action item.
[04:58] Carlos: about fallback, what exactly happens if we hit the abort gate at 5%? is it instant rollback or gradual throttle?
[05:06] Liam: we recommend immediate traffic steering back to hosted fallback with a short cool-down — we can do gradual if you need graceful degradation but immediate rollback reduces blast radius.
[05:17] Tom: how seamless is fallback routing? do we keep session continuity?
[05:20] Rina: session continuity depends on where the session state lives; if client retains conversation state, steering to hosted keeps prompts intact. if you rely on local KV in dedicated infra, some state might be lost — need to instrument.
[05:36] Priya: so we need a session mapping and sticky routing doc.
[05:40] Jordan: we'll draft a sticky routing appendix in the runbook.
[05:44] Priya: monitoring — what dashboards and alerts should we expect?
[05:47] Liam: per-route latency, per-model token counters, GPU util, KV hit ratio, batching window histograms, per-customer cost burn rate. alerts: p95/p99 drift, error rate, sudden drop in KV hit ratio.
[06:02] Sofia: we need audit logs to tie request ids to customer ids for compliance.
[06:07] Maya: yes, we'll include request-id tracing across the pipeline and a retained audit log export (30/90/365 days options).
[06:15] Carlos: any specific note about sequence length distribution? we saw long tail beyond 8k tokens in the canary.
[06:21] Liam: for extremely long sequences we recommend truncation policy and streaming responses to reduce cold token cost; also consider prefix compaction.
[06:30] Elena: can we run an AB test on truncation policy? like compare local truncation to server-side streaming?
[06:36] Rina: yes we can run AB within the canary lanes. that'll be a separate 2-variant test.
[06:42] Priya: let's make sure to include user experience owners for the AB metrics.
[06:46] Maya: good call.
[06:48] [10:12] 
[10:12] Liam: i pulled a preliminary run of 3 variants last night: baseline, micro-batched, quantized-8. baseline p95 420ms, micro-batched p95 390ms but p50 increases slightly, quantized p95 480ms but cost down 32%. p99s were noisy — we need longer runs to stabilize.
[10:32] Priya: those numbers help. for patient chat we need to keep p95 <= 500ms so quantized might be acceptable if kept in background only.
[10:40] Maya: what about A/B scorecard metrics? suggestions?
[10:43] Elena: besides latency, track conversion to appointment booking, session completion rate, and NPS for in-app chat.
[10:50] Liam: we'll add business metrics hooks to the telemetry so you can map model variant to downstream KPIs.
[10:56] Carlos: infra note — the spike correlated with a metadata store GC on our side around 2:30 into the run, so we need synchronized quiet windows for tests.
[11:04] Tom: yes we will schedule a maintenance-free window next Tuesday 02:00-08:00 PT for the host perf run.
[11:11] Rina: reminder: when doing host-run there may be slight perf difference from dedicated due to network topology, we'll annotate the spreadsheet with expected delta.
[11:21] Sofia: security again — retention windows and access for audit copies, can Redwood support per-tenant retention config?
[11:27] Maya: yes per-tenant retention available, and we can provide S3 export to your audit bucket with KMS encryption.
[11:34] Priya: any red flags on SLA side if we do dedicated?
[11:38] Liam: SLA is tied to Reserved capacity purchases; dedicated gives lower variability. we're proposing a 99.9% target for p95 in dedicated plans for interactive, but contract can be adjusted.
[11:49] Elena: we want to rehearse runbook — can team walk through step-by-step?
[11:53] Jordan: quick walkthrough: pre-cutover checklist (smoke tests, monitoring ready, rollback playbook), stage ramp with gates, telecon‐ops channel creation, escalation paths, post-cutover validation checklist. we'll run a dry rehearsal on Aug 6.
[12:10] Priya: during the rehearsals can we simulate partial rollback to test data consistency?
[12:15] Rina: yes we can script synthetic traffic with failure injection to validate rollback.
[12:20] Tom: what about blue-green vs canary, which do you recommend?
[12:23] Liam: canary for gradual exposure and easier instrumenting, blue-green if you need atomic swap and quick rollback; both have tradeoffs. for this workload canary is safer.
[12:35] Priya: last question from me — billing visibility during ramp, we need live cost dashboards.
[12:39] Maya: console provides token-level cost and burn rate; we'll share a sample dashboard and give you access to a cost-study view.
[12:46] Carlos: technical question: when you do model quantization is it per-variant or dynamic at runtime?
[12:50] Liam: quantization is per-built variant; you deploy a quantized artifact and we route to it. dynamic swapping is possible but requires extra orchestration.
[12:58] Elena: who signs off on the go decision?
[13:01] Priya: product + ml + security + ops, so Elena, Priya, Sofia, Tom together.
[13:07] Maya: ok we'll set a go/no-go checkpoint doc for Aug 10.
[13:11] Rina: small note — make sure telemetry retention long enough for historical baselining during the 20% stage.
[13:17] Priya: agreed.
[13:19] [Growling phone, crosstalk for a sec]
[13:25] Maya: any outstanding blockers?
[13:27] Carlos: main blocker is VPC peer access and temporary window for host perf test.
[13:31] Sofia: and final KMS constraints for HSM rotation.
[13:35] Maya: good, we'll chase those in action items.
[13:38] Jordan: recap of next steps: Liam perf sheet, Maya security docs & pricing delta, Carlos grant test window, Jordan schedule rehearsal, decision meeting Aug 10.
[13:50] Priya: sounds good. thanks all.
[13:53] Maya: thanks team, will follow up in email with the runbook link and calendar invites.
[14:00] [Meeting ends]
